title: The Mayan Palace
project: A haunted Mayan palace in the deep Mesoamerican rainforest (the Petén lowlands of Guatemala): a story cue from curious exploration to a chase and a narrow escape
brief: a Hans Zimmer-style, cinema-grade 7.1.2 score of at least 2 minutes 30 seconds: a hero explores a haunted ancient Mayan palace in the deep rainforest of the Petén, opens a relic out of curiosity and frees an evil, is chased through the palace and then the deep forest, and escapes narrowly using his own power. No sound effects: pianos, orchestra, percussion and voices tell the chase; only the ambience of a haunted palace (with bats) and of the forest is heard
audience: a listener on an 8-channel (7.1) system or headphones who should feel they are in the chase; they came for the story
purpose: a 185-second cue that tells a whole story: wonder, discovery, a mistake, a chase and an escape
point_of_view: the explorer: the steps and the forest touching the runner are the nearest sounds; the palace and what it holds are what is closing in
job: let the first half be curiosity with a low pulse under it, so the opening of the relic lands as a mistake the listener saw coming
hold pressure from bar 26 to bar 66 with a pulse that does not stop; the only rest is the bar before it
turn the minor key to major only at the escape, so the power is heard as a change and not as a reward
story: An explorer walks into a stone palace, slow and curious. In a small chamber they find a carved relic, touch it and open it. Something inside is released; a door shuts behind them and for one bar there is nothing. Then they run: through the corridors with a stone guardian behind, through a collapsing exit and into the night forest where branches and leaves tear at them and trees break behind. Cornered, they turn the curse back with a power of their own and escape by a hair. The forest is calm again and the question has an answer.

sections.name: the_entry
sections.action: an explorer walks into a stone palace the forest has swallowed, torch-lit, curious and unafraid
sections.music: a D pedal in the basses, a far timpani stroke, a high shimmer in the strings, a piano that asks a six-note question, and a far closed-mouth hum that answers

sections.name: the_relic_chamber
sections.action: the explorer finds a carved relic in a small chamber, studies it, touches it and opens it
sections.music: the question comes back up a fourth, a bass clarinet answers it from the stone, a harp touches the relic, a cello pulse grows under, a choir cluster appears, and a stone lid grinds open

sections.name: the_opening
sections.action: what was inside is out: the palace wakes, a door shuts behind the explorer
sections.music: a braam, a choir cluster that climbs a semitone a bar, the question in the horns as a threat, a death whistle far inside the walls, a chant that starts on the beat, then one full bar of nothing

sections.name: the_corridors
sections.action: the chase through the palace corridors: the explorer runs, a stone guardian follows, the way out collapses
sections.music: a piano pulse of sixteenths that does not stop, chop strings, a 3+3+2 drum pattern with a snare, trombone stabs, a heavy low piano octave behind for the pursuer, the chant on the beat, the horns state the threat, and a timpani roll and a cymbal for the exit falling in

sections.name: the_forest
sections.action: out into the night forest, running through leaves and branches, with the pursuer breaking trees behind
sections.music: the pulse continues a tone higher with fast violin runs for branches and leaves, a bar with a beat of silence and a rush for the stumble, the violins climb a semitone a bar, and a hit on the first beat after a rest each time the pursuer breaks a tree

sections.name: the_escape
sections.action: cornered, the explorer turns the curse back with a power of their own and escapes by a hair
sections.music: the minor key turns to D major, the hero theme in the horns overrules the threat, and one last hit lands

sections.name: the_release
sections.action: the power spent, the explorer is out of reach; the monsters stop and the forest is quiet again
sections.music: the last hit, a beat of nothing, then a held low D, strings in D major and the horns' hero theme at half weight, a conch far away

sections.name: the_aftermath
sections.action: the forest at night, calm; the explorer is safe, and the reed holds a low, steady D
sections.music: a held D major, the flute's question answered and falling home to D, the forest returns, and the bass clarinet holds a low D

motifs.name: the relic motif
motifs.shape: D Eb D A G F: a flat second that returns, a leap of a fifth, then a falling step (it ends on F, not home on D: a question)
motifs.returns: in the flute as a question (bar 4), up a fourth (bar 9), in the bass clarinet as the answer (bar 11), in the horns as a threat (bars 18-61), in the flute again as a resolved answer (bar 70), and answered at last, falling home to D

motifs.name: the hero theme
motifs.shape: D A C D E D C A: a rising fifth, a climb to the octave and a step above it, then back down; over D major the C natural keeps a hard-won mixolydian colour (the flat seventh) instead of a plain major lift
motifs.returns: once more at bar 66 a fourth higher, and under the aftermath as a held horn D

pulse: the relentless pulse is a piano figure of sixteenths with staccato celli and violas from bar 26 that never stops until bar 66; before it there is only a warning: one far timpani stroke per bar from bar 5, a sparse cello figure of eighths from bar 13 (the relic hum), and a rolled timpani in the opening; footsteps are the second pulse; a 3+3+2 drum pattern from bar 26

gate_reason: a build-hit-release cue with a long melodic line (the motif), a held bar and a release: the cinematic profile, started strict
notes: Every field is a target someone can check. feel and avoid_feel are what listen.py tests earshot against; sections is the cue's arc in seconds, and its names are what a trajectory or a room change is anchored to; hits_at is what listen.py looks for in the onset list, and hits is the same moments with a reason and a kind (cut, motion or musical). spatial_staging is the room seen from above: each preset must match its own spot. immersive says whether the field is doing a job, what moves and why, and where the room changes (numbers live in the presets). mix_intent says what must be audible and what must stay free. Write in plain English: earshot reads the words.

expression.sonic_picture: The first ten seconds are a low D held on a piano in a large dark room with bats in the vault and far away a whistle, and a high piano that is close and a little hesitant asking a six-note question; the middle is a hard, fast run, a piano pulse of sixteenths with fast violin runs on both sides and a heavy low octave behind; the last note is a low reed holding D under a wide major chord.
expression.performer: The flute breathes before the long note and lets the last note fall off; the celli dig into the beat with a little drag on beat one and a push into the next bar; the horns enter late on the threat and play the leaps with a short slide in; the timpani stroke is soft and slightly behind; the pianist plays the pulse with the left hand a hair ahead and trips once, in the bar with a beat of silence.
expression.producer_moves: The room gets bigger at the opening and tighter in the corridors and then opens to the forest; one full bar of nothing before the chase; the tempo accelerates in the chase and the forest; a single tutti hit and one beat of nothing before the release; the key turns to major only at the escape.
expression.anti_generic: The generic version is a drone, a riser and a drum loop with a monster sound; this one is a story told by a motif that is first a question, then an answer, then a threat, and is finally overruled by a different shape, with a pulse that appears only once the evil is out.

theme.contour: a flat second that returns, a leap up of a fifth and then a falling step: a question that does not resolve
theme.interval_character: a minor second, a perfect fifth, two steps down
theme.rhythm_cell: long, short, long, very long, long, long
theme.why_memorable: the semitone returns before the leap, so the ear expects the fall to land on D and it lands on F
theme.variation_plan: up a fourth and curious in the flute, low and hollow in the bass clarinet, loud in the horns as a threat, overruled by the hero theme in D major, and finally answered in the flute, falling home to D
